transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-12-10
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Alex Carter (Redwood AE), Maya Singh (Redwood SE), Tom Ruiz (Redwood CSM); Dr. Emily Park (CTO, Synapse), Ravi Sharma (Head of ML), Lena Ortiz (Procurement), Carlos Mendez (Eng)

Summary: Short scoping call to align on POC commercial guardrails and technical success criteria, agree test harness and timeline for benchmarks, and outline procurement path.

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex Carter: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm alex from redwood, i'll kick off. hey emily, ravi, lena, carlos, good to see you all. this is a scoping to get the poc terms sorted — credits, duration, success metrics and the bench marks we need to run.
[00:18] Dr. Emily Park: thanks alex. we want to validate performance and cost on our clinical summarization workload, and make sure there's no surprises with PHI handling and procurement.
[00:35] Ravi Sharma: yeah, mainly two things: 1) throughput for our nightly batch (about 100k docs / month) and 2) p99 latency for interactive clinician queries, target under 200-300ms per response ideally.
[00:50] Maya Singh: quick clarifier, are the interactive queries single-turn short prompts or multi-turn chat? that affects tokens per call and cache behavior.
[01:05] Ravi Sharma: mostly single-turn but can be a couple turns, average 150 tokens per request, peaks to 800 tokens for longer summaries.
[01:22] Alex Carter: got it. for a pilot we typically propose a 90-day window with an initial credit allotment — example: $10k credits covering hosted API usage plus up to X reserved throughput for a short bench run. we can adjust based on the benchmark.
[01:40] Lena Ortiz: procurement question — does the pilot require a PO or is it on net-30 invoice after pilot? we need to see T&C and any trial agreements.
[01:55] Tom Ruiz: for pilots we do a lightweight pilot agreement / MSA addendum. usually no full contract needed to start the bench, but procurement often wants an outline of commercial guardrails: credit cap, allowed usage, data handling. we can do a pilot SOW that states credits, duration, and acceptance criteria.
[02:18] Carlos Mendez: on infra, do you support VPC peering or private endpoints? we need traffic to stay inside our VPC for any PHI-related flows.
[02:33] Maya Singh: yes, Redwood Private and Dedicated options support VPC peering and on-prem packages. for hosted pilots we can arrange a private endpoint plus KMS integration for key control; we'll include specifics in the security packet.
[02:50] Dr. Emily Park: important: legal will flag PHI, so we need encryption at rest + in transit and explicit statement that we won't store customer PHI beyond cache TTLs.
[03:05] Tom Ruiz: understood. i'll include SOC2 cert, KMS/HSM notes, and our retention and audit log practices.
[03:20] Ravi Sharma: back to success criteria — we want to define quality metrics, e.g., F1 on entity extraction >= 0.92 on our validation set, and latency p99 under 400ms for interactive. also cost per 1M tokens target so we can project run costs.
[03:40] Alex Carter: that sounds reasonable — success criteria should be measurable: throughput (docs/hr), latency p50/p95/p99, quality thresholds on labeled eval set, and cost run rate. we'll capture those explicitly in the pilot SOW.
[03:58] Lena Ortiz: how do credits work — are they dollar credits off invoices or strictly for API usage? we need to see how they apply in case we go to Dedicated later.
[04:13] Alex Carter: credits are applied to usage on the hosted account. if you decide to migrate to Dedicated, credits can be applied toward initial committed spend — we'll outline treatment in the term sheet.
[04:28] Dr. Emily Park: timeline — we want the pilot to start before year-end if possible; procurement calendar might push to January. what's a realistic schedule for the bench and contract?
[04:43] Tom Ruiz: procurement usually 2–4 weeks for a small PO; legal review for data sensitive customers can be 4–6 weeks. but we can run the benchmark privately with a test account while contracting runs in parallel.
[05:00] Maya Singh: for the benchmark i suggest we run two phases: 1) baseline functional correctness and quality on a 2k example subset, 2) stress tests for throughput and latency on a synthetic scaled set that mirrors your nightly batch. we'll provide a harness (we have a small runner) and can instrument metrics.
[05:22] Ravi Sharma: the stress test should emulate our distribution: 80% short prompts (150 tokens) and 20% long summaries (600-800 tokens), plus 10% concurrency spikes around midnight.
[05:40] Maya Singh: noted. also want to call out prefix/KV cache behavior — it may change effective latency for multi-turn flows. we can test with and without cache.
[05:58] Alex Carter: commercial guardrails — example structure we typically propose: 90-day pilot, $10k credit for API usage, bench support credits (one-time), max throughput reserved for 48-hour benchmarking window, success criteria defined, and path to procurement with a draft SOW.
[06:20] Lena Ortiz: does that $10k cover dedicated infra or only hosted? and are there limits on test data size?
[06:35] Alex Carter: it covers hosted usage. Dedicated has separate reserved commitments and would be part of a separate commercial discussion if the pilot proves out. test data size we'll agree on — usually we ask for a representative subset for quality plus synthetic scaling for throughput.
[06:50] Carlos Mendez: network egress costs — we need clarity on who pays for egress during bench runs if using cloud region outside our tenancy.
[07:05] Tom Ruiz: we'll include region info and estimate egress in the term sheet; if there's a Dedicated/private deployment, egress is handled according to the provisioned infra.
[07:20] Ravi Sharma: benchmarks: can you share prior examples for similar healthcare customers? we want to set expectations on tokens/sec and cpu/gpu footprints.
[07:34] Maya Singh: yes, we have anonymized benchmark decks; i'll share a condensed sheet with tokens/sec, p50/p95/p99 numbers on models we typically recommend. note that model choice (e.g., quantized variant) will impact latency and cost. sometimes we recommend a slightly smaller model to meet latency SLOs.
[07:55] Dr. Emily Park: model governance — if we see hallucination regressions during the pilot, what's the rollback path?
[08:09] Alex Carter: we support A/B rollouts and automatic fallback to a conservative model variant. we'll also help with prompt engineering and evals to track regressions. part of the pilot will include eval suites you define.
[08:22] Ravi Sharma: on metrics capture, will we get token-level cost and per-route dashboards? that's important for us to correlate costs to features.
[08:35] Tom Ruiz: yes, Redwood Console provides per-route cost, latency breakdowns, and trace hooks — we'll enable a dashboard for the pilot.
[08:48] Carlos Mendez: technical detail: can we run the benchmark with GPU-accelerated instances? we prefer to test with hardware similar to production footprint.
[09:00] Maya Singh: for hosted pilots we can provision burst dedicated nodes for the benchmark window; for Dedicated you'll have fixed GPU pools. we'll document the kernel selection behavior and quantization profile used.
[09:16] Lena Ortiz: from procurement perspective, what's the path post-pilot? we need a clear path to a SOW and PO or an enterprise contract.
[09:29] Alex Carter: typical path: pilot SOW -> pilot completes & acceptance -> commercial proposal for Dedicated or hosted agreement -> PO and MSA. Redwood's legal team provides a pilot addendum to the MSA to reduce review time.
[09:45] Dr. Emily Park: acceptance criteria example — quality threshold on labeled eval set, throughput sustained above X docs/hr for 4 hours, and p99 latency under threshold for interactive. if those are met we consider pilot successful.
[10:05] Ravi Sharma: can we include a clause about data deletion post-pilot and auditability? that's non-negotiable for PHI work.
[10:18] Tom Ruiz: yes, we'll add data deletion and audit log exports to the SOW and include an ACL for retention.
[10:30] Alex Carter: i'll put together a draft commercial guardrail doc today: credit amount options (10k/25k), pilot length options (60/90 days), and a sample acceptance matrix.
[10:43] Maya Singh: technical deliverables i'll provide: benchmark harness repo link, sample metrics dashboard, instructions for VPC peering or private endpoint, and a checklist for KMS integration.
[11:00] Dr. Emily Park: good. on scheduling: let's aim to have the draft term sheet and security packet by end of week. procurement will review and flag any special clauses.
[11:12] Lena Ortiz: i'll feedback on procurement timeline and whether we can issue a PO quickly. my target is to have preliminary internal OK by 2025-12-16.
[11:25] Carlos Mendez: small note — we may want a short live demo of the Console for our ops folks; can we slot that after the benchmark?
[11:38] Tom Ruiz: absolutely, we'll do a Console walk-through aligned with reports from the benchmark run.
[11:50] Alex Carter: ok, recap of next steps: i'll send the POC commercial guardrails and credit options, maya will share benchmark harness and previous anonymized benchmarks, tom will send security docs, emily and ravi will confirm dataset and acceptance tests, lena will share procurement timing. follow up meeting week of 2025-12-22 to review results.
[12:15] Dr. Emily Park: sounds good, thanks everyone.
[12:22] Alex Carter: thanks all, we'll follow up with the materials. bye.
[44:05] (call end)

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings around product names (Redwood Dedicated spoken as "Redwood Dedicate"), and abbreviations; filler words and interruptions present.
